title: Yara and the Autopsy
premise: Insurance investigator Casper Coldharbour is assigned the claim of Yara Voss, a lighthouse keeper's daughter declared dead after vanishing from the coastal town of Greyhollow. When he obtains her diary and finds entries written weeks past her disappearance, he realizes either Yara lives or someone is forging a dead woman's hand — and both possibilities point to the town's founding family, whose inheritance hinges on her death certificate. Casper's search for the 'dead' witness everyone protects unearths a found family of outcasts who kept Yara hidden to shield her from the man who tried to kill her. In the end, Casper must choose between loyalty to the people who saved Yara and the truth that will cost them everything: he testifies just before the statute expires, Yara is legally resurrected, the inheritance is redirected to the found family's clinic, and Casper burns his photographic memory's archive to let Greyhollow keep its secrets.
about_author: Emrys Ishikawa is the pen name of a former marine insurance adjuster who spent eleven years investigating deaths at sea before turning to fiction. They live in a converted fog-signal station on the Oregon coast, where they write mysteries about paper trails that refuse to stay cold.

chapters.title: The Claim File
chapters.summary: Casper Coldharbour, POV. An insurance firm assigns Casper the contested death-in-absentia claim of Yara Voss; he memorizes the file in one reading, noting an inconsistent tide chart. Emotional beat: professional detachment masking a hunger for a case that finally resists him.

chapters.title: Greyhollow Welcomes You
chapters.summary: Casper POV. He arrives in the fog-bound town and interviews the harbormaster, who is warm until Yara's name surfaces, then suddenly precise and empty. Emotional beat: first taste of a community performing grief like choreography.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Ledger
chapters.summary: Casper POV. At the decommissioned lighthouse he meets Odile, Yara's aunt, who hands over the missing woman's effects including a water-stained diary. Emotional beat: tenderness tangled with something that looks like fear.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Casper POV. Reading the diary by lamplight, Casper finds dated entries continuing three weeks past the disappearance — describing a storm, a boat, a name half-blotted. Emotional beat: vertigo; his perfect memory now holds two impossible timelines.

chapters.title: The Statute Clock
chapters.summary: Casper POV. His supervisor warns him the legal presumption-of-death window closes in forty days; after that, the Voss estate settles permanently with cousin Aldous Voss. Emotional beat: the case becomes a countdown.

chapters.title: Aldous at the Wake
chapters.summary: Aldous Voss POV. The heir hosts a memorial dinner, charming donors while privately burning a letter; he notices Casper watching. Emotional beat: polished menace, the reader learns what Casper only suspects.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: Casper POV. Door-to-door interviews yield identical phrasing — 'poor Yara, God rest her' — word for word across nine households. Emotional beat: uncanny uniformity; a town rehearsed like witnesses.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Silence
chapters.summary: Tomas, a retired ferryman, POV. Tomas remembers rowing a hooded passenger the night Yara vanished but has told no one for seven years. Emotional beat: guilt as a stone carried so long it feels like part of the body.

chapters.title: Photographic
chapters.summary: Casper POV. Casper reconstructs the memorial guest list from memory and spots a face that appears in no official record — a young woman photographed looking not at the coffin but at him. Emotional beat: the hunter realizes he is being hunted gently.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Back
chapters.summary: Nell, the mystery woman, POV. Nell follows Casper to warn him off, leaving a note signed with a drawing of a gull instead of a name. Emotional beat: protective hostility hiding desperation.

chapters.title: Diary Forgery or Diary Truth
chapters.summary: Casper POV. A document examiner confirms the late entries are in Yara's authentic hand — no forgery possible. Emotional beat: relief curdling into dread; if she wrote them, why does everyone need her dead?

chapters.title: What the Tide Took
chapters.summary: Odile POV. Flashback chapter: Odile recalls the night her brother, Yara's father, drowned — officially an accident, officially witnessed by Aldous. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into silence.

chapters.title: The Gull Society
chapters.summary: Casper POV. Following Nell, Casper discovers a shuttered cannery housing a scrappy free clinic run by outcasts — the found family at the story's heart. Emotional beat: warmth breaking through fog.

chapters.title: Patients Without Papers
chapters.summary: Dr. Imani Okafor, clinic founder, POV. Imani treats people the town pretends don't exist and recognizes Casper as a threat to all of them. Emotional beat: fierce hospitality with a locked door behind it.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Small Kindnesses
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, rotating short scenes. The clinic's members each recall one act of quiet aid they gave a woman who never gave her name. Emotional beat: the reader assembles Yara from fragments before Casper can.

chapters.title: Aldous Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Casper POV. Aldous offers Casper a consulting retainer and hints the insurer prefers certainty over truth. Emotional beat: temptation framed as reasonableness.

chapters.title: The Blotted Name
chapters.summary: Casper POV. Under raking light, Casper recovers the blotted diary name: 'D—' followed by a tide time matching the night his own father's fishing boat was lost near Greyhollow. Emotional beat: the case turns personal without permission.

chapters.title: Casper's Own Drowned Year
chapters.summary: Casper POV. Flashback: teenage Casper watched investigators close his father's drowning in nine days with tidy paperwork. Emotional beat: understanding why he became a man who reads files like autopsies.

chapters.title: Dead Witness Walking
chapters.summary: Nell POV. Nell reveals she saw the attack on Yara — that she is the witness everyone swears is dead, legally erased when Aldous had her declared lost at sea years ago. Emotional beat: terror finally given a shape and a name.

chapters.title: Why the Town Lies
chapters.summary: Harbormaster Brann POV. Brann confesses the town's complicity: Aldous holds their mortgages, their jobs, their histories. Emotional beat: cowardice explained, never excused.

chapters.title: Halfway Mark: The Storm Cellar
chapters.summary: Casper POV. In the lighthouse storm cellar Casper finds supplies restocked within the last year — someone has been living there recently. Emotional beat: hope with wet footprints.

chapters.title: Yara Wrote Past Her Death
chapters.summary: Yara POV (first appearance). Hidden chapters of the diary in Yara's voice: the attack, the rescue by strangers, her choice to stay dead so the clinic would inherit what Aldous couldn't touch. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed from the grave.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Casper POV. Casper decodes the will: if Yara's death is confirmed before the statute expires, the estate passes to Aldous; any credible evidence of life freezes it entirely. Emotional beat: the diary isn't a message — it's a legal weapon.

chapters.title: Someone Read the Diary First
chapters.summary: Casper POV. The diary pages show handling by a second person; Casper reconstructs from fiber traces and ink offset that Aldous read it and returned it, gambling no one would look. Emotional beat: the predator has been inside the evidence all along.

chapters.title: Brann Breaks
chapters.summary: Brann POV. Confronted with the ferry log, Brann admits he falsified the tide chart under pressure from Aldous. Emotional beat: a small man choosing, at last, a large truth.

chapters.title: They Know He Knows
chapters.summary: Casper POV. Casper's rental is searched, his notes photographed, a dead gull left on his windshield. Emotional beat: fear arriving as punctuation.

chapters.title: Imani's Bargain
chapters.summary: Imani POV. Imani offers Casper a deal: the clinic will produce Yara alive if he can guarantee the statute testimony shields them from prosecution for harboring her. Emotional beat: trust negotiated between people trained to expect betrayal.

chapters.title: The Dead Witness Testifies to Herself
chapters.summary: Nell POV. Nell drafts her statement — identity papers, the erasure, the night she watched Aldous strike Yara and roll her toward the water. Emotional beat: a ghost signing her own resurrection.

chapters.title: Aldous Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Aldous POV. Aldous moves up the estate hearing, hires the examiner's rival to discredit the diary, and schedules the cannery's demolition permit. Emotional beat: villainy as administration.

chapters.title: Forty Days, Day Thirty-Nine
chapters.summary: Casper POV. On the eve of expiry, the clinic's plan collapses — Yara refuses to surface, believing her death protects them more than her life would. Emotional beat: the case's true antagonist revealed as love shaped like sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Argument in the Storm Cellar
chapters.summary: Yara POV. Casper finds Yara and argues the only way to save the found family is to stop hiding inside its lie. Emotional beat: two stubborn survivors negotiating what safety costs.

chapters.title: What Casper Remembers
chapters.summary: Casper POV. Casper offers his photographic memory as corroboration — every page, every date, every forged initial — knowing recall alone may not be admissible. Emotional beat: a gift that cannot be taken back.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Before the probate judge, Nell testifies, Brann recants, and Aldous's counsel dismantles the diary's chain of custody. Emotional beat: truth losing on procedure.

chapters.title: The Statute Expires at Midnight
chapters.summary: Casper POV. With minutes left, Casper recites the diary verbatim from memory, then produces the one thing no one disputed: the tide chart in Aldous's own archived handwriting. Emotional beat: triumph delivered flat, exhausted, human.

chapters.title: Yara Stands Up
chapters.summary: Yara POV. Yara walks into the courtroom alive, ending her own death with four words: 'I'm here. He did it.' Emotional beat: catharsis earned across thirty-four chapters.

chapters.title: Aldous Unravels
chapters.summary: Aldous POV. Cornered by the tide chart, the ferry log, and his own burned letter's surviving carbon, Aldous confesses to his father's drowning and the attempt on Yara. Emotional beat: a man discovering his empire was made of signatures.

chapters.title: What the Law Can't Return
chapters.summary: Casper POV. The court restores Yara's name and redirects the estate; but the clinic faces exposure, and the town's complicit majority wants it all sealed. Emotional beat: victory with a bill attached.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: Casper POV. The town demands Casper suppress his testimony against Brann and the others; he refuses the cover-up but negotiates leniency, splitting the difference between the two things he serves. Emotional beat: integrity as compromise rather than purity.

chapters.title: The Archive Burns
chapters.summary: Casper POV. Casper destroys his reconstructed memory-file of the town's smaller sins, keeping only what justice required. Emotional beat: a man teaching his perfect mind mercy.

chapters.title: Yara and the Autopsy
chapters.summary: Ensemble final chapter. One year later: the clinic thrives in the renovated cannery, Yara tends the relit lighthouse, and Casper, staying on as its pro bono administrator, opens a new claim file — alive this time. Emotional beat: found family formalized; the autopsy was never of a body, but of a town's silence.
